platform.summary: Fishback ran in the 2026 Republican primary for Florida governor on a 'Florida is full / Florida first' affordability and land-protection message: ban data centers statewide, abolish homestead property taxes for residents, keep Wall Street and out-of-state money from buying Florida homes, and end the H-1B 'scam'. He also ran as the anti-donor, anti-developer candidate (he refuses foreign-affiliated money and says rivals want to 'pave over every inch' of Florida) on top of a conventional conservative base (pro-life, Second Amendment, backing police, school choice).

planks.title: Ban data centers statewide
planks.promise: Ban AI/hyperscale data centers in all 67 counties through statewide preemption of county approvals, to protect farmland, water and electric bills.
planks.tells_for: Votes or stated positions to ban, put a moratorium on, or preempt data-center approvals; opposing data-center rezonings on farmland/ag land; refusing data-center-industry money.
planks.tells_against: Votes to approve or fast-track a data center, rezone ag land for one, or give it tax breaks; campaigning on attracting data centers/AI infrastructure.

planks.title: Eliminate homestead property taxes
planks.promise: Eliminate property taxes on Florida residents' homesteads (not snowbirds, Airbnb owners or mega-estates), paid for by rolling local government spending back to 2021 levels.
planks.tells_for: Votes for homestead exemption increases, assessment caps or abolition (e.g. the 2026 Save Our Homes amendment); pledges to cut or end homestead taxes; pledges to cut local spending/millage.
planks.tells_against: Votes or statements for raising millage or property taxes; opposing homestead tax relief; defending local government revenue growth.

planks.title: Florida homes and land for Floridians
planks.promise: Ban private equity/Wall Street firms from buying single-family homes (and force divestment of the 117,000 they own), tax out-of-state vacation-home buyers $50,000, and keep foreign adversaries from owning Florida land.
planks.tells_for: Supporting limits on institutional or foreign buyers of homes and land (e.g. SB 264 foreign-land limits); proposing taxes or caps on out-of-state/investor purchases.
planks.tells_against: Opposing limits on corporate/foreign land buying; courting institutional or foreign real-estate capital.

planks.title: Slow growth, protect land and water
planks.promise: Develop 'slower and smarter', stop overdevelopment that 'paves over every inch' of Florida, continue Everglades restoration and conserve state parks and waterways ('Florida is full').
planks.tells_for: Votes or statements to hold or tighten the urban growth boundary, require approvals for large developments, deny rezonings of farmland/open space, fund conservation/Everglades; refusing developer money.
planks.tells_against: Votes to expand the urban boundary, waive development oversight, preempt local growth limits, approve large developer land deals over resident objections; heavy developer funding.

planks.title: Florida workers first: end H-1B
planks.promise: End the H-1B 'scam' with fines that wipe out any savings from replacing a Florida worker, keep H-1B workers off state contracts, raise foreign-student tuition, and back strong immigration enforcement and deportations.
planks.tells_for: Votes or statements for state cooperation with federal immigration enforcement, E-Verify, detention of criminal illegal immigrants, limiting H-1B/guest-worker displacement of Americans.
planks.tells_against: Votes or statements against immigration-enforcement bills; defending H-1B/guest-worker expansion or sanctuary-style policies.

planks.title: No foreign or big-donor money
planks.promise: Refuse contributions from foreign-affiliated groups (naming AIPAC) and run against donor capture: calls frontrunner Byron Donalds a 'slave' to donors and says he does not need $100 million to run.
planks.tells_for: Stated pledges to refuse foreign-linked, corporate-PAC, developer or out-of-state big-donor money; small-dollar funded campaigns.
planks.tells_against: Documented reliance on developer, foreign-linked or mega-donor/PAC money; stated openness to it.

planks.title: Back police, restore order
planks.promise: Raise pay and restore a pension COLA (and 20-year retirement) for law enforcement and corrections officers, end teen takeovers with felony charges, surge state resources on homelessness, and remove prosecutors who refuse to prosecute.
planks.tells_for: Votes or positions raising penalties for rioting/disorder, funding or improving pay/pensions for officers, supporting police, tough-on-crime prosecution.
planks.tells_against: Votes cutting officer pensions/benefits; opposing penalties for public disorder; defund-style positions.

planks.title: Defend the Second Amendment
planks.promise: Eliminate Red Flag laws, end the war on suppressors/bump stocks/FRTs, and repeal the 2018 law that raised the long-gun purchase age to 21; also pull Flock cameras and stop Palantir contracts.
planks.tells_for: Votes for permitless carry, stand-your-ground, against the 2018 post-Parkland gun law, against red-flag laws; pledges to oppose new gun restrictions.
planks.tells_against: Votes for the 2018 age-21/waiting-period law, red-flag laws, assault-weapon or magazine limits.

planks.title: Pro-life, no exceptions
planks.promise: Life begins at conception; shut down Florida's abortion clinics and replace them with crisis pregnancy centers, plus paid maternity leave.
planks.tells_for: Votes or statements for the 6-week or 15-week bans, waiting periods or other abortion restrictions; support for pregnancy centers.
planks.tells_against: Votes or statements against abortion restrictions; support for abortion-access measures.

planks.title: School choice and teacher pay
planks.promise: Universal school choice (fund Step Up toward dollar-for-dollar parity with public schools), a Homeschool Commissioner, and a 25% raise for teachers.
planks.tells_for: Votes or statements for vouchers/charters/universal choice and for raising teacher pay.
planks.tells_against: Votes or statements against voucher/charter expansion or school-choice funding.

HJR 1-F (2026F).why: Amendment 3 raises the homestead exemption and lowers assessment-increase caps: a homestead property-tax cut, in the direction of Fishback's plank (though short of elimination).

SB 180 (2025).why: Bars local governments in storm-hit areas from adopting stricter development rules, i.e. preempts local growth limits; Fishback runs against overdevelopment. Caveat: the bill also contains legitimate emergency-management provisions.

SB 2-C (2025C).why: State cooperation with federal immigration enforcement.

SB 1718 (2023).why: E-Verify for larger employers plus immigration-enforcement measures.

HB 675 (2016).why: Requires state/local compliance with federal immigration law; bans sanctuary policies.

H.R. 29 (2025) Laken Riley Act.why: Mandatory detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft/burglary/assault of an officer; state suits over enforcement.

SB 264 (2023).why: Restricts land purchases near military sites and infrastructure by people from China and other countries of concern.

HB 1 (2021).why: Combating Public Disorder: raises penalties for riot-related offenses (Fishback: felony rioting for teen takeovers and mobs).

SB 2100 (2011).why: 2011 Florida Retirement System overhaul that ended the cost-of-living adjustment for service after July 1, 2011; Fishback promises to restore a COLA for officers. Medium confidence: roster text says only 'FRS changes'.

SB 7026 (2018).why: Parkland law raised the long-gun age to 21 and created a waiting period; Fishback pledges to repeal it.

CS/SB 7026 (2018) Marjory Stoneman Dougl.why: Same 2018 law Fishback pledges to repeal (age 21, waiting period).

SB 128 (2017).why: Stand Your Ground burden-of-proof shift to prosecutors.

HB 5 (2022).why: 15-week abortion ban (Fishback wants more, same direction).

HB 633 (2015) Informed Patient Consent.why: Adds a 24-hour waiting period before an abortion.

CS/HB 7069 (2017) Education.why: Expands charter-school capital funding and options; Fishback backs charter and choice expansion.

Aqua by the Bay stipulation (2020).why: Yea removed a county-board approval requirement on a large development once 750 units were built, i.e. waived development oversight.

Override of Mayor Levine Cava's veto of.why: Yea let a 378-acre industrial project outside the Urban Development Boundary proceed, over the mayor's veto.

Introduction of the 99-year Terra/Frisbi.why: Yea advanced a 99-year developer lease of public land over residents' objections (voters later rejected it about 74% to 26%).

score = round(100 * (# planks with +1) / (# planks with evidence)), only when 2+ planks have evidence; otherwise null. It measures alignment with Fishback's platform on documented items only, not candidate quality. A candidate with 2 evidenced planks can easily read 0, 50 or 100: show the plank count next to the score.

When a legislator has several votes on the same plank, the plank match is the sign of the summed votes; ties are left out. Roll-call votes outrank manual statements for the same plank. 'Not voting' and 'Excused' are ignored.

Bill mapping judgment calls: SB 180 (2025) and the local developer votes (Aqua by the Bay, South Dade logistics override, Boca 99-year lease) count AGAINST slow-growth-protect-land; SB 2100 (2011, FRS overhaul that ended the COLA for service after 7/1/2011) counts against back-police-order with medium confidence; HJR 1-F (2026F, Amendment 3) counts FOR end-homestead-tax as a partial step; SB 7026 (2018) and its CS version count AGAINST second-amendment because Fishback pledges to repeal it; HB 7069 (2017) counts for school choice as a charter-expansion bill.

Unmapped on purpose (no clear plank): HB 1-D redistricting, all budgets (HB 5001, SB 2500, H.R. 5371, H.R. 7148, H.R. 1968), SB 2-A and SB 4-D insurance/condo bills, HB 3 (2024), the SAVE Act, OBBBA, NDAA, H.R. 881, H.R. 152, HB 1557, HB 7 (2022), HB 43, HJR 1 (2017), SB 736, HB 1355, HB 7013, HB 7015, HB 7101, the Hialeah street co-naming and the Boca term-limit charter amendment.

Priority-1 and priority-2 candidates had no entries in the roster votes list, so their evidence is from campaign sites (Jolly, Donalds, Simpson, Green, Hoolihan, Fitts, Varnadore), forum coverage (Tampa Bay Beacons, WLRN) and the roster's own research record. Evidence marked url '' came from the roster record text, which carries no URL; treat those as researched but not re-fetched.

Wilton Simpson reads 100 on seven planks from his own site and record (farmland easements, SB 264, pro-life, Back the Blue, sanctuary-city ban, Arms and Ammo Act, school choice) but there is no documented stance from him on data centers or homestead elimination, and his record also includes the sugar-grower lawsuit shield and the ag-labor immigration feud that are not scored.

Byron Donalds scores 67: +1 end-homestead (pledge to push elimination), +1 workers-first (E-Verify, deport criminals), -1 stop-data-centers (opposes a statewide moratorium, though says locals can reject them).

Amanda Ballard's land record is net negative (2023 wetland-buffer cut, 2026 Mosaic extension, partly offset by the Mixon Fruit Farms purchase); her donor list includes two affordable-housing developers. Tara Poulton accepted money from one PAC and says none from developers, so clean-money is left out for her.

No usable plank evidence found: Bellamy, Moody (1 plank), Nixon, Gillespie, Jewett, Dimanche, Datto, Davis, Bradenton council candidates (only generic 'responsible growth' language, except Green's police-budget pledge), Mosquito Control, West Manatee Fire district, most CDD and local candidates.

Not done: roll-call votes for priority-1 legislators from before the roster (e.g. Jose Javier Rodriguez, Ingoglia, Donalds in the Florida House or Congress) were not pulled; this is the main place to add evidence if time allows.
